Definition: from G4862 and G5143 (including its alternate); to rush together (hastily assemble) or headlong (figuratively):--run (together, with).
BiblicalUsage: As the lame man who is healed holds Peter and John, all the people run together to them in Solomon's porch, greatly wondering, and the people see the disciples departing, and many know Him, and run afoot out of all cities, and outgo them, and come together to Him. Running together is the crowd's response to a wonder, and the wonder is what draws them: a healed man and a departing boat are enough to set a whole city running.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that wonders still make people run together, and I hold that a healed lame man is a better sermon than any invitation.
